title: EFC Perturbation Sector: Constraint-Driven Gravitational Slip and a Testable Lensing Crossover
description: This note presents the perturbation-sector prediction of Energy-Flow Cosmology (EFC) for weak-lensing amplitude as a function of redshift, summarized by an effective ratio eff(z) relative to a CDM baseline set to unity. EFC predicts a single redshift crossover at z ≃ 0.44 separating enhanced (eff > 1) from suppressed (eff < 1) lensing, with percent-level deviations bounded at approximately ±2% over 0.2 ≲ z ≲ 1.4. The result is posed as a sealed, falsifiable target for upcoming weak-lensing tomography.

cdm_baseline.description: CDM reference for the effective lensing amplitude ratio eff(z), as indicated by the "CDM (= 1)" baseline.

efc_crossover_condition.description: EFC predicts a crossover redshift where the effective lensing matches CDM, near z ≈ 0.44.

efc_percent_bound.description: Percent-level EFC deviation band (±2%) over the plotted redshift range, separating enhanced (above 1) and suppressed (below 1) lensing regions.

key_results.main_finding: EFC predicts a weak-lensing efficiency ratio eff(z) that crosses unity at z ≈ 0.44 with deviations confined to about ±2% over 0.2 ≲ z ≲ 1.4, implying enhanced lensing below the crossover and suppressed lensing above it relative to CDM.

sealed_predictions.statement: A single sign-changing crossover in the weak-lensing efficiency ratio eff(z) relative to CDM occurs at z ≈ 0.44, with enhanced lensing (eff > 1) at lower z and suppressed lensing (eff < 1) at higher z.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Tomographic cosmic-shear and galaxy–galaxy lensing measurements (e.g., DES, KiDS, HSC, LSST, Euclid) that reconstruct the redshift dependence of the lensing amplitude ratio relative to CDM.

sealed_predictions.statement: Across 0.2 ≲ z ≲ 1.4, the magnitude of the deviation in eff(z) from unity remains within ±2%.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: High-precision weak-lensing tomography and joint analyses with CMB lensing that constrain percent-level deviations in the lensing amplitude as a function of redshift.

kill_criteria: KC1: No crossover of eff(z) near z = 0.44 is observed—specifically, if tomographic weak-lensing measurements show no crossing within 0.30 < z < 0.55 at ≥3σ significance.

KC2: The measured deviation of eff(z) from unity exceeds ±2% anywhere within 0.2 < z < 1.4 at ≥3σ, or remains on one side of unity across the entire range at ≥3σ, contradicting the predicted sign change.
KC3: Independent tomographic CMB lensing or joint cosmic-shear × CMB-lensing reconstructions show a crossover redshift inconsistent with 0.44 by more than Δz ≈ 0.1 at ≥3σ.

ledger_impact.holistic_analysis: This paper delivers the first sealed, quantitative perturbation-sector prediction for EFC weak lensing: a single crossover in eff(z) at z ≈ 0.44 with ±2 % bounded deviations over 0.2 ≲ z ≲ 1.4. It fills the previously empty perturbation/lensing prediction slot, gives Stage-IV surveys (Euclid, Rubin LSST, Roman) a concrete falsifiable target, and directly services KC4 (lensing observables) by providing the sealed numerical envelope against which forthcoming tomographic cosmic-shear data will be compared. No KC is closed—the predictions await data—but the prediction side of KC4 is now locked.
graph_insights: No existing papers or validation tests were found within 1–2 hops, confirming this is the first perturbation-sector document in the EFC graph; it seeds a new sub-cluster (lensing/perturbation) that future cosmic-shear and CMB-lensing nodes will attach to.

The concepts 'redshift crossover' and 'percent-level deviation' are new graph nodes; they will become shared connection points once the EFCLASS Boltzmann solver and the Euclid/Rubin rapid-response pipelines are added, linking the theory-gap and engineering-gap branches.

The absence of connected validation tests underlines that pipeline actions (action-6, action-7 both PLANNED) should prioritise a lensing-specific verification script analogous to the RSD rapid-response pipeline flagged in the biggest-gap note.

implicit_consequences: The ±2 % amplitude bound implicitly constrains the EFC coupling function ξ(a) at the perturbation level far more tightly than the background fit alone; any future modification to ξ(a) that survives background tests but violates this lensing envelope is pre-falsified.

A crossover at z ≈ 0.44 in eff(z) implies a corresponding, correlated signature in the galaxy–galaxy lensing ratio and in the Σ(z) = Φ+Ψ Weyl potential growth rate, meaning additional independent observables (e.g., DES Y6 or KiDS-1000 galaxy–galaxy lensing) become indirect tests of the same prediction without a new sealed deposit.

Because eff(z) > 1 at low z, EFC predicts a slightly higher S₈ when inferred from shear below z ≈ 0.44 and a slightly lower S₈ above it, providing a natural, parameter-free explanation for the observed S₈ tension trend between low-z and CMB-calibrated analyses.

The percent-level deviation envelope means that any EFCLASS Boltzmann solver (theory-efclass-boltzmann-solver gap) must achieve sub-percent numerical accuracy in the lensing kernel to be useful for verification—this tightens the solver specification.
The three paper-internal kill criteria (KC1–KC3 of the paper) map onto sub-tests under the project-level KC4, but do not retire KC4 itself; KC4 remains SEALED until Stage-IV data arrives.
